title: Passion Fruit Curd
subtitle: Intensely fragrant, sharp tropical curd with real depth
excerpt: Passion fruit curd uses fresh passion fruit pulp, seeds and all, strained to give a vivid yellow, intensely aromatic curd. Lemon juice sharpens the set. Makes two small jars.
sourceNotes: Pam Corbin, Preserves. Passion fruit has high tartaric acid, the curd sets firmly and needs less lemon juice than berry curds.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freezes well for up to 3 months. Defrost in the fridge overnight and stir before using.

glossaryTerms.definition: A heatproof bowl set over a saucepan of barely simmering water, so the steam heats the bowl gently. Used for delicate emulsions like curd where direct heat would scramble the eggs.

content.text: Passion fruit curd has a vivid yellow colour and a perfumed, distinctly tropical sharpness that lemon curd can't match. Fresh passion fruit are essential,  the pulp is strained to extract juice and straining removes most of the seeds, though a few strands will remain. Makes about two 200 g jars.

items.prepNote: wrinkled ones are sweetest and most fragrant

content.text: Halve the passion fruits and scoop the pulp into a fine sieve set over a bowl. Press and push the pulp firmly with the back of a spoon to extract the juice. You need about 80 to 100 ml. A few jelly-covered seeds can be left in if you like texture; strain everything out for a completely smooth curd.
Put the passion fruit juice, lemon juice, sugar, and butter in a heatproof

a pan of barely simmering water. Stir until the butter melts and the sugar dissolves. Add the beaten eggs and stir constantly for 15 to 20 minutes until the curd thickens and holds a line on the back of the spoon. The water must stay at a simmer, not a boil.
Pour through a fine sieve into hot sterilised jars. Seal while hot and allow to cool completely. The curd will thicken further as it cools.

items.symptom: Curd has a bitter, chemical note
items.cause: Overcooked, passion fruit aroma compounds are volatile.
items.fix: Remove from heat as soon as the curd coats the spoon. Prolonged cooking drives off the fragrance and can bring out bitterness.

items.symptom: Not enough juice from 8 passion fruits
items.cause: Unripe fruits have less juice and less flavour.
items.fix: Use wrinkled, heavy fruits, they are ripe and fully juicy. Smooth, light passion fruits can be almost dry inside.
Pass through a fine sieve; the texture usually recovers. Next time, keep the water at a bare simmer and stir without stopping.

items.symptom: Seeds are visible in the finished curd
items.fix: Pass through a fine-mesh sieve twice if seeds are a concern. This is aesthetic only, seeds don't affect flavour or shelf life.

content.text: Refrigerate immediately. Use within 4 weeks. Freezes for up to 3 months.
